identityReview: Rahul Gandhi, born 19 June 1970 to Rajiv Gandhi and Sonia Gandhi; Congress politician, fifth-term Lok Sabha MP for Rae Bareli and Leader of Opposition effective 9 June 2024. He is not currently Congress president or prime minister. Wayanad resignation effective 18 June 2024 and announced 24 June; outdated party biography is not used for current constituency. Rollins undergraduate graduation 1994, Cambridge Development Studies MPhil 1995, Harvard attendance without graduation. The 2019 public resignation letter is distinct from the earlier offer; 2023 conviction stay and parliamentary restoration are not final acquittal.
lifeStatusEvidence: Times of India’s 18 November 2026 report describes his actual Columbia University appearance on Tuesday, 17 November, with remarks and the BJP response. Indian Express and the dated party event page corroborate a separate 14 November Hyderabad speech. Neither a planned Chicago visit nor page crawl time is used as proof of attendance. No original video was viewed.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read party historical biography, independent legislative profile, contemporary degree-confirmation and resignation reporting, a reproduced Supreme Court interim order, two official Gazette notifications, relevant sections of a parliamentary session report, and recent speech reporting. Read candidate and parent Commons metadata, exposing conflicting licence and date descriptions. Portrait bytes unavailable.
corrections: Read Congress’s historical biography: birth 19 June 1970 to Rajiv and Sonia Gandhi; Rollins undergraduate degree in 1994 and Cambridge MPhil in 1995; consulting work before politics; first election in Amethi in 2004; AICC general secretary on 24 September 2007; vice-president in January 2013; party president from 16 December 2017. Its four-term/Wayanad current-office wording is outdated and replaced with PRS and parliamentary records. The May 2019 resignation shorthand is distinguished from the 3 July public letter. Bharat Jodo Yatra ran from 7 September 2022 to 30 January 2023. Organisational growth, social benefits and party claims of success are not independent findings; exact march length and participation totals are omitted.

Read PRS’s 18th Lok Sabha profile: elected Congress MP for Rae Bareli, Uttar Pradesh, fifth term, term start 9 June 2024, current Leader of Opposition. Parliamentary activity coverage ends 13 August 2026, not the crawl date. The page explains that the opposition leader does not sign the attendance register, so N/A is not absence or zero attendance. PRS is an independent legislative-research organisation, not the parliamentary secretariat. Current office is also corroborated by November reporting. Party membership counts shown in navigation are not reused as certified election results.

Read the 29 April 2009 agency report in The Indian Express describing Cambridge Vice-Chancellor Alison Richard’s confirmation: Trinity College attendance October 1994–July 1995 and MPhil in Development Studies awarded in 1995. This is reporting of a university confirmation, not an original degree certificate or directly inspected university letter. The degree is not a PhD, and attendance at Harvard does not establish a Harvard degree. No unsupported degree subject for the Rollins bachelor’s qualification is added.

Read Xinhua report of 3 July 2019: Gandhi publicly released his resignation letter and accepted political responsibility for the general-election loss. A 25 May resignation offer had been rejected by party colleagues. The report also confirms losing Amethi and winning Wayanad in the same election. The timeline dates publication of the letter, not a separately certified party-committee acceptance or successor’s installation. Resigning as party leader was not resignation from Parliament. Electoral defeat is not treated as proof of every criticism of his leadership.

Read the Supreme Court’s 4 August 2023 order as reproduced in LiveLaw’s PDF, including operative paragraphs 10–13 rather than only its editorial headnote. The Court stayed the conviction during the appeal; it did not decide the merits or acquit him. It discussed the lack of reasons for imposing the maximum two-year sentence and consequences for representation, while also criticising the remarks. The reproduced text/headnote uses 1950 for the Representation of the People Act; the official parliamentary notification cites 1951, so the profile avoids repeating the apparent year error. No current disposition of every later proceeding is inferred.

Read Gazette S.O. 3512(E), dated 7 August 2023: Supreme Court relief on 4 August concerned the Surat trial judgment of 23 March, and disqualification notified on 24 March ceased to operate subject to further judicial pronouncements. This is parliamentary restoration following a stay of conviction, not final acquittal, an expunged trial history, or a finding about unrelated litigation. The exact original disqualification notice was referenced by this official notification rather than independently opened.

Read Gazette S.O. 2457(E), dated 26 June 2024: the Speaker recognised Rahul Gandhi, Congress leader in the Lok Sabha, as Leader of Opposition with effect from 9 June 2024 under section 2 of the 1977 statute. The effective date is separate from the June party announcement, the 26 June notification and the 27 June announcement in the House. This office is not Speaker, prime minister or Congress president.

Read relevant sections of the Lok Sabha Secretariat’s September 2024 resume of the 18th Lok Sabha first session, especially printed pages 11–12: Wayanad seat resignation effective and accepted on 18 June 2024, announced in the House on 24 June. The later Speaker-announcement table records opposition-leader recognition on 27 June. Session dates were 24 June–2 July; those dates do not replace effective appointment dates. The full publication’s unrelated tables were not audited, and no claim that he now represents both Wayanad and Rae Bareli is made.

Read Indian Express report updated 15 November 2026 describing the Saturday, 14 November Bharat Summit speech in Hyderabad and platform-worker activities that day. It establishes an actual speech, not merely an advertised event. Assertions about electoral manipulation, business influence, democracy and future electoral victory remain Gandhi’s political claims. No independent voter-roll analysis, criminal finding, verified insurance payout or completed national policy is inferred. Embedded media were not watched. The party event page corroborates the date and title but did not expose a complete transcript.

Read Times of India report updated 18 November 2026 describing his Tuesday Columbia University appearance, hence 17 November, and employment/education remarks. It also reports the BJP’s rebuttal; neither side’s political characterization is adopted as an independent economic finding. The closing reference to a scheduled Chicago event calls 18 November Tuesday, although the calendar date is Wednesday. No Chicago attendance or future outcome is inferred from this inconsistent scheduling sentence. No full event video or university transcript was reviewed.

Read relevant body paragraphs of The Indian Express’s 19 June 2023 education and pre-politics explainer, despite subscription-interface text elsewhere on the response. It corroborates Rollins graduation in 1994, Cambridge MPhil in 1995, Harvard attendance without graduation, Monitor Group work and first Amethi election in 2004. Its discussion of citizenship controversy is not evidence of British nationality; the profile makes no such claim. A linked Rollins alumni listing and original company filings were not separately inspected. No private school or degree records examined.

additionalConsulted.access: Search returned a biographical preview, but opening supplied no usable biography body. Not presented as a fully read source; dated Gazette and parliamentary publications plus PRS supply the relevant claims.
Read date and event heading confirming a 14 November 2026 address. A video was embedded but not watched, and the web body did not contain the full speech transcript suggested by the search preview.

Read 3 July 2019 PTI report confirming public insistence on resignation and earlier 25 May offer rejected by party colleagues. This corroborates chronology, without certifying the party’s final formal acceptance date.

Read linked parent’s own-work declaration, CC BY-SA 4.0, photographer, 13 October 2022 date and 20 March 2024 upload. No pixels inspected; the candidate’s CC BY-only notice and different date are not silently accepted.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified human or native-language review. No original degree certificate or Cambridge letter, complete election audit, party resignation acceptance record, exhaustive later litigation review, event video, Chicago attendance evidence, portrait bytes or confirmed crop permission chain. Political allegations and economic predictions remain attributed; the 2023 order is described as a historical interim decision, not a certified statement that all proceedings remain pending in 2026.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages checked for 19 June 1970 birth, fifth Lok Sabha term and Rae Bareli constituency; 18 June 2024 Wayanad resignation versus 24 June announcement; 1994 Rollins graduation/1995 Cambridge MPhil versus Harvard attendance; 2004 parliamentary entry, 24 September 2007 party post, January 2013 vice-presidency and 16 December 2017 presidency; 25 May 2019 resignation offer versus 3 July public letter and Amethi loss versus Wayanad win; 7 September 2022–30 January 2023 march; March 2023 conviction/disqualification versus August stay/restoration; 9 June 2024 effective opposition leadership versus 26 June notification; actual 14 and 17 November 2026 activities, attributed allegations and no inferred Chicago attendance.
